properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/18/2025 to APEX ENERGY (PA) LLC in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: APEX ENERGY (PA) LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/18/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8222091
Permit API: 129-29262
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/18/2025
Comments: Inspection 1 of 2:On February 18, 2025, the DEP conducted a two part Incident Inspection of the Herminie Well Site (ESCGP-3 issued: 12/12/2024, expires: 12/11/2028), located in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 2/14/2025 by CNX representative Mr. Andrew. The spill report states that as CNX dug into the well pad to install secondary containment and production equipment, water and diesel fuel filled the hole. Refer to Part 2 of this inspection for details on soil samples that were collected at the time of this inspection.At the time of this inspection, the Herminie Well Site has reportedly been acquired from Apex Energy by CNX.At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 sign was at the access road entrance and inside the onsite mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, all of which had Apex Energy's name and information on it. The access road which was graveled appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. Once on the well pad, the DEP was accompanied by CNX representatives, Mr. Andrew, Chad Eisenman, and Carrie Crumpton. Mr. Andrew informed the DEP that at the time of this inspection, operations were in the drill out phase, fracking was completed last week and flowback would be starting next week. Mr. Andrew showed the DEP the spot where the first hole was dug, the DEP observed a partially frozen red substance mixed with what appeared to be frozen water that was giving off a strong petroleum based odor. Mr. Andrew stated that several test holes were then dug until CNX found a point in each direction where the fluid was no longer observed, this determined the extent of the impacted area, which appeared to approximately 60ft x 90ft with 8 total holes marked with cones to identify them as contaminated.At the time of this inspection, Penn E and R was on site with plans to excavate the area and place all contaminated material into a roll off dumpster on site. CNX could not provide the DEP with an approximated quantity of this release, but theorized that it may be over 42 gallons and plans to follow Act 2 protocol for this release. Once contaminated material is excavated, CNX hopes to have a more definitive quantity for the release. At the time of this inspection, the DEP inquired whether CNX believed any waters of the Commonwealth were impacted and Mr. Eisenman explained that the pad has catch drains all around the perimeter which discharge into an infiltration basin on the back right corner of the well site. Mr. Eisenman also stated that all catch drains and discharge points are routinely plugged during all Alteration Operations and that they were closed prior to CNX discovering the substance in these holes. The DEP also inquired when CNX hypothesizes the spill occurred, Mr. Andrew and Mr. Eisenman both stated that they believe the spill occurred when Apex Energy was operating the well pad (According to Department records, Apex Energy has not reported a spill at the Herminie well site regarding diesel fluid in this area of the well pad).Due to the spill reportedly occurring prior to CNX acquiring this well site, at the time of this inspection, the DEP collected soil samples to determine what the substance may be and to determine if this substance reached the infiltration basin prior to the drains being plugged. Refer to Part 2 for details on the collected soil samples.CNX is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations, and how CNX quantified the amount spilled.CNX will need to follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and CNX is requested to assess the impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the release.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for a release on the well pad.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/19/2025 to KRIEBEL NATURAL GAS CO LLC in Manor Borough, Westmoreland county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: KRIEBEL NATURAL GAS CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/19/2025
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8225648
Permit API: 129-28077
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Borough
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/19/2025
Comments: On March 19 2025 the Department conducted an inspection of the RWS Development 001 OG Well in regards to an incident reported to the Department of an explosion and fire at the well site on 3/19/2025 at 1:00 pm. Present during the inspection were several representatives from the Manor Volunteer Fire Department, Westmoreland City Fire Department, Jay Niehenke (Kriebel), Ronald Seich (Kriebel) Ben Dickun (Kriebel) and Charles Reaggle (DEP).-This is inspection 1 of a 2 part inspection-The findings are as follows:Upon the Department's arrival to the well site, no active fire was observed. The Department spoke to fire department representative Brian Williams who stated they used approximately 3200 gallons of municipal water from their firetruck as well as Dawn Dish Soap at a 0.6% per gallon concentration to extinguish the fire on site. While onsite, the SDS sheet for Dawn Dish Soap used was sent to the Department electronically by the Fire Department Representative Brian Williams. According to the SDS sheet, "Ecotoxicity- The product is not expected to be hazardous to the environment."Upon inspection of the production equipment, the Department observed damage to the equipment including a hole in the production tank as a result of the incident. Upon inspection of the hole in the production tank, the Department observed a small intermittent trickle of fluid from the production tank hole, down the side of the tank to the ground. A soil conductivity reading was taken directly under the hole in the tank with a reading of OR (over detectable range, >20.0 mS). The Department inquired what the most recent tank level was prior to the incident. Mr. Dickun stated that it was believed to be approximately 2 feet 6 inches from the bottom, however the date and exact measurement was unknown as that information is stored on a computer and was unable to be accessed at the time of the inspection. The Department took a measurement of the of the hole in the tank, which appeared level with the fluid level and obtained a measurement of approximately 2 feet 10.5 inches. While onsite, a truck arrived and began emptying the fluid from the production tank.The Department then assessed the well site to determine impacts resulting from any releases on the site as a result of the explosion/ fire and resulting measures taken to extinguish it. The Department observed a ditch/channel approximately 15 feet behind the well. The ditch appeared to run approximately 180 feet where it terminates just before a stream. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. The Department also observed absorbent pads in the ditch that were reportedly placed placed by the Fire Department. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of OR, 6.28mS, 5.75mS, and 5.25mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. Conductivity readings were taken in this area of the ditch with readings of 0.42mS, 0.34mS, and 0.42mS.The Department then took conductivity readings of the water in the stream. A conductivity reading was taken upstream of where the ditch appears to terminate with a reading of 0.65mS. There appeared to be a large amount of debris and trash in the stream and on the stream bank upstream where this conductivity reading was taken. A conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.90mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/10/2020
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 902029
Permit API: 125-28620
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Robinson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/10/2020
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 12/10/2020 at approximately 2:15 PM. The operator reported that an open top buster tank overflowed during flow back operations and approximately 20 gallons impacted the ground behind the tank. The operator reported a total of approximately 188 gallons total was spilled, with 168 gallons spilling to secondary containment. The operator is reporting that the spill will be remediated in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1). Nate Smiell and Brandon Carson with Range are on site, on my arrival. The following is observed: The site is currently in flowback operations (Photo 1). The pad drain has been closed. According to Mr. Smiell, he identified the spill at approximately 12:15 PM on 12/10/2020 during a routine inspection of the site. A time for the incident could not be provided at the time of this inspection. Mr. Smiell stated that it could have occurred anywhere between 12 and 24 hours prior to it being found. According to Mr. Smiell the open top tanks are to be inspected and the contents measured every hour. The Department requests these inspection logs be provided for the 24 hours preceding when it was found. Additionally, the Department requests the secondary containment logs for the past month, and at what time was the secondary containment remediated with the vacuum truck? Mr. Carson stated that it was possible that on-site cameras may have recorded the incident. The Department requests more information on this, whether they were able to record the incident and at what time the incident occurred if it was recorded. SPSI is on site and prepping to begin remediation of the site impacted by the spill. The Department requests photographs of the site post clean up as well as the waste manifest once it becomes available. The Department recommended to Mr. Smiell that the operator increase the length of the secondary containment (Photo 2 & 6). Based on this inspection, violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending the operator's response, more violations may be forthcoming.

On October 16, 2025 DEP received a certificate of well plugging for the well. Upon review, DEP observed the well had been plugged utilizing multiple mechanical plugs that did not appear to be located within 20’ of a stratum bearing or having borne oil, gas, or water consistent with ¿¿78.92(b). Additionally, the well was cemented solid to surface with no vent, contrary to the venting requires of ¿¿78.92. The certificate of well plugging was checked for the box "The well was plugged by a DEP approved alternate method pursuant to section 78.75 or 78a75." On October 30, 2025 DEP began inquiring with EQT to confirm the manner in which the well was plugged. EQT confirmed the well had been plugged as indicated on the October 16, 2025 certificate of well plugging. DEP informed EQT it had not secured alternative methods to do so. Further, EQT did not install a vent consistent with ¿¿78.92(b)(5), which refers to the venting requirements of ¿¿78.92(a)(3). Violations of ¿¿3221 and ¿¿78.75 have occurred due to EQT failing to request and receive approval for alternative methods to plug the well as it did. Due to a technical error, the violations cannot be cited in this application.

Comments: On March 16, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Ziolkowoski Well Site (NOT approved on 11/6/2023) in regard to a release reported to the Department on 3/15/2026 (CTS 395839). Present during the inspection was operator representative Nick Reda.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of inspection, there are 14 total wells on the well pad. Wells (2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, 6H, 7H, 8H, 9H, 1H,10H,11H,12H, and 14H) appeared equipped for production with well tags present. Mr. Reda stated they are currently swapping out equipment to complete flowback operations on the 13H.Upon inspection, all necessary drilling equipment appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No fluid leaks or spills were identified around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks and GPUs appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Reda guided the Department to the location(s) of the reported release. According to Mr. Reda the release occurred on 3/15/2026. He stated the release was caused by a scrubber malfunction on a third-party water truck. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of produced water released to the graveled access road.The Department observed the location(s) of the release and remediation. It appeared the area of the release was split into two different sections of the access road. Mr. Reda said due to the malfunction of the scrubber on the water truck, the release occurred only on the steep portions of the access road. Therefore, the release began approximately halfway down the access road, ceased as the truck reached a level area, and then continued to release on another steep section towards the bottom of the access road.Upon inspection of where the release began, the Department observed an area where impacted material was excavated from the access road (photos 12-13). According to Mr. Reda, the release in this area of the access road was about 150 feet in length and about 1 foot in width. Small puddles of rainwater were observed in this section of the access road. Conductivity readings of 0.49mS, 0.24mS, and 0.43mS, were obtained in the area of the release/remediation. These readings appeared comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.60mS obtained in the gravel on the side of the access road near the well pad entrance (away from the spill and heavy vehicle traffic). Prior to leaving the site, the area of excavation was backfilled with clean gravel (Photos 23-24).Upon inspection of where the release continued near the bottom of the access road, the Department observed fresh gravel (Photo 17). Mr. Reda stated the impacted material had been removed and the area of excavation had been backfilled. Mr. Reda stated the release in the area of the access road was about 180 feet in length and about 1 foot in width. Conductivity readings of 0.12mS, 0.15mS, and 0.23mS were obtained in the area of the release/remediation. These readings appeared comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.60mS obtained.Mr. Reda stated all impacted material was placed into 3 roll-off boxes (photos 21-22) and would be disposed of properly. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued as immediately corrected for the observed release as it appeared to be remediated in accordance with current regulations (78a66).

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/18/2021
Comments: Site inspection conducted to review residual waste processing activities at the EQT COP 551B pad with EQT Company Man Bill Mitchell. Weather at time of inspection is partly sunny and 46 degrees F. According to Mr. Mitchell, Precision Drilling Rig #110 is currently drilling the 6H well at a depth of 6378'. This is the 7th well of 9 total to be drilled during this setup. Drilling resumed on the 6H well on 10/15 and the well is being drilled using Water Based Mud to kickoff point at 8650' where the rig will be switched over to Synthetic OBM. The anticipated Total Depth of the 6H well is 22897'. All nine wells have been batch drilled to the intermediate depth. The 7H well was recently completed and cemented on 10/13. Clean Harbors Backyard Crew is processing the drill cuttings in the rig backyard. Three shale shakers and three drying shakers are active. Polymer flocculant is being added to the drilling mud during this inspection before it is run through the centrifuge. One centrifuge is removing cuttings from the drilling mud. An excavator is mixing wood pellets into the drill cuttings to solidify the material for landfill disposal. Prior to site transfer to EQT, ARD submitted a Request for Approval for Previously Approved Alternative Waste Management Practices (OG71) Form B for this well pad on 2/2/2021. The Department approved the request on 2/3/2021. The intent of onsite drill cuttings processing is to separate the solid fraction of the cuttings from reusable drilling mud fluid so fluids can be returned to mud tanks for further drilling activity. For further information, refer to the COP Tract 357 Pad A OG-71 Form A application regarding drill cuttings processing (EFACTS authorization #1300435). During this inspection, fluid with a sheen is observed within tertiary containment outside the OBM tanks. The Department recommends that containment structures be vacuumed and fluids be sent for treatment or disposal. The original trench sump collecting runoff along the access road near the mud tanks has a field conductivity reading of 733 uS/cm. There Re no new violations noted during this inspection. Violations remain outstanding on Pad B based on Inspection Report #3231577 by DEP WQS Brad Kline dated 8/9/21.

Comments: On June 14, 2024 the Department conducted a Routine Inspection of the Joseph A Negri 1 well located in East Huntington Township, Westmoreland County. During a previous inspection (IR 3723492) the Department observed a drum on site with a Methanol label on it. At that time the Department requested the operator provide information by 3/29/24 on what exactly is in the drum and what it is being used for, the Department also requested that the Operator remove all equipment not necessary for production. The Department has not received a response from the Operator in regards to this site.At the time of this inspection, the well site was exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues observed. A well tag with all required information posted on it was fixed to the wellhead. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead. Some production equipment onsite that appeared to be in production due to the gauge attached to it had an open pipe close to the ground. A soil conductivity reading was taken at the edge of the well site in some vegetation as a background (0.0074 mS) and then a reading was taken directly next to the piping (0.409 mS) and then a little further back from this piping (0.382 mS). The production tank also had some wet marks coming from the top of the tank and the wet marks can be seen going down the tank towards the ground in areas. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the base of the production tank below areas where the wet marks were observed on the tank (0.1483 mS and 0.1405 mS). The drum of methanol was observed to still be on site, not in secondary containment and fluid can be seen sitting at the top of it with air bubbles forming from what may be a small hole or crack in the top of the barrel. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the base of the drum (0.096 mS), as well as in the fluid sitting at the top of the drum (0.620 mS).The soil conductivity readings taken near the open pipe and at the base of the production tank are elevated in comparison to the background soil conductivity reading and subjugate that there is some sort of release contaminating the soil in both areas. The reading at the base of the Methanol drum is comparable to the background, but the fluid sitting at the top and the air bubbles seen indicate that there may be a leak at the top of the drum which currently has the potential to reach the ground. While onsite, the Department spoke with Dave Lindahl of Mountain View to let him know about the elevated readings by the production equipment and production tank and informed him about the possible hole at the top of the Methanol Drum. The Department recommended the drum be removed or put in secondary containment as soon as possible and recommended they determine how the two leaks occurred, stop them, remove all contaminated soil, replace it with new top soil, and seed/mulch. Dave stated that someone would be onsite on 6/17/24 to begin working on all of this. The Department is recommending the Operator either remove this drum or put it within secondary containment by COB June 28, 2024. Based on todays inspection, violations shall be issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not currently in use and for a release from production equipment.

properties.content:
Report Details

Permit API: 129-26159
Unconventional: No

Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to IR 2997935 conducted on 2/14/2020 in which violations were issued. The entirety of the site was walked due to a pad lock on the gate (Photo 2). The access road still appears to be rutted which in several locations has allowed for the creation of accelerated erosion channels (Photo 1, 6, 11, 12, 13, 16, 17, & 27). Straw bale barriers still appear to be installed incorrectly and not properly maintained (Photo 4, 5, 9, 10, 14, 15, 18, & 19). The access road is still pooling water at low spots, this has created the potential for sediment discharges leaving the site (Photo 3, 8, 14, 18). In several locations the water has been standing long enough for tad poles to occupy them (Photo 20). No E&S Plan was found on site. Per the E&S Plan received in the operator's response dated 2/24/2020 and created in 2006, it appears that at least one culvert that was installed is not depicted on their plan, nor is it installed to the details set forth in that E&S Plan (Photo 7). Per 102.4(b)8 the E&S Plan must be available for review at the project site during all stages of earth disturbance activity. The access road and well pad do not have adequate temporary stabilization, nor have they achieved a minimum uniform 70% vegetative cover (Photo 1, 8, 11, 12, 13, 16, 22, 24, & 25). Down slope controls at the well site, do not appear to have been installed (Photo 23). Based on this inspection, violations will be issued as reoccurring for potential for discharge, and failure to have the site temporary stabilized, additional violations will remain outstanding.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted against permit 081-21855 for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from 12/19/22.

Violation ID: 8202009

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2024
Comments: On September 18, 2024 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well Site located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3774486 where violations were issued for an 18-20 barrel release of production fluid from a production tank on June 4, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the production tank that was leaking during IR 3774486 has since been removed from the well site. A well tag was fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it, and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges was observed coming from or near the wellhead. The area where the production tank once (where the spill originated), the slope that the spill traveled down, and the area downstream where the spill pooled up at now appears to be backfilled, seeded and mulched pending vegetative growth. In addition, at the edge of the downslope area right before a forested area began, some black fencing was observed.Several soil conductivity readings were taken in the spill areas (0.0418 mS, 0.0362 mS, 0.0054 mS, 0.0137 mS, and 0.0602 mS) and are significantly lower than the soil conductivity readings taken in the same areas at the time of the spill (Soil conductivity readings taken on 6/4/24 documented in IR 3774486: 1.35 mS, 1.454 mS, Over Range, 7.63 mS, 5.51 mS, and 4.90 mS). Upon inspection of the fence, two areas appeared to be compromised. A stake appeared to be snapped and the fence appeared to be pushed down by sediment, at this time, there did not appear to be any evidence of the sediment overtopping the fence and no erosion or sedimentation was observed behind this section of fence. Another section of the fence right behind a small tree appeared to not be trenched and a gap was observed between the bottom of the fence and the ground. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed behind this section of the fence a this time either.The Department is recommending the Operator promptly properly implement and maintain the temporary erosion and sedimentation (E and S) best management practices (BMPs) to prevent any pollution from occurring.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly implement and maintain E and S BMPs. In addition, violations issued during IR 3774486 shall remain outstanding until the Act 2 Report is submitted, received, reviewed and approved by the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

Comments: On May 20 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the CFR USX 5 OG Well in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4157445.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department again observed the water flowing onto the access road. It did not appear any remedial actions have been taken to address the flowing water and resulting erosion and sedimentation issues on the access road.The water was observed flowing down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water. The water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Comments: This site located north off Apple Orchard Road in a brushy, heavily vegetated area. Well is set-up for production with a meter, separator and one tank in secondary containment. Will Warfel, with Diversified Energy LLC, reported on October 5 at 2:53 a release of ~5 barrels of produced fluid from a patched plug in tank, into secondary containment where the tank was set.
